Impossible to be correct is 294 ⟦2⟧; for of the covering of the feet by the garment (when sitting or however) ⟦3⟧ is entirely unsuitable, since it means "roofing over" or "roofed over", from ⟦4⟧ (⟦5⟧), cf. also Arist. ⟦6⟧. 1294 of the tortoises: ⟦7⟧ . . ⟦8⟧. (Also ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧, which Weil recalls, is quite well understood from this sense.) So whoever is in the open air, as Athena must be when she ⟦11⟧, is ⟦12⟧, and so it seems ⟦13⟧ should be written instead of ⟦14⟧. ⟦15⟧ as Pindar Ol. 13, 72 ⟦16⟧, cf. the same Frg. 167 of Caeneus ⟦17⟧. — To seek here an allusion to the battles of the Athenians in Egypt is, because of the spatial distance between Egypt and Libya, entirely inadmissible.

On the plains of Phlegra, the scene of the Gigantomachy, see Preller-Robert Myth. 75 (⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧. ⟦6⟧. 1194, ⟦7⟧ Ar. ⟦8⟧. 824). ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧, ⟦11⟧; naturally this localization of the Gigantomachy comes from the same poets for whom Olympus was the mountain of the gods. On this scene of their battles (against Enceladus ⟦12⟧) the goddess gladly dwells.
